result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req071-mount-auth-tenant-status-plugs.md. Confirmed via direct code reading (api_pipeline.ex:28-31, router.ex:42-50, auth_pipeline.ex, tenant_status.ex:58-59) that AuthPipeline/TenantStatus are already correctly mounted, ordered, and that TenantStatus's Repo.get/2 call has no rescue (OQ-14's fail-closed claim is real, not aspirational). Designed 5 end-to-end test specs (through Letflow.Router / Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus, not the plugs standalone) covering AC1-AC5, exact moduledoc replacement text for both plugs (AC6), and the exact code REVIEWER must check plus the exact stage-4-api-surface.md insertion point for AC7.

issues.description: This run's Step 00 handoff (context.requirement_text) paraphrased REQ-071's acceptance criteria as 6 items, understating the real 7 in docs/requirements.yaml -- AC4 (migrating POST 503 + equivalent GET 200) and AC5 (concurrent lookup-failure isolation) are two separate criteria there, not one. Design doc §1a documents the correction; no functional impact since this design used the real text throughout.

Genuine AC-wording gap, not a code defect: AC2 ("reaches the handler") and AC4's GET-200 half assume a real tenant-scoped business handler exists. REQ-070's ten sub-routers are all stub match-all-404 routers by design (owned by later REQ-073+ requirements), so no end-to-end test today can produce a literal 200/real-handler-reached result without inventing a fake production route (forbidden by this run's scope). Design doc §1 (AC2, AC4) documents substituted, honest assertions (404-not-401/503, no Retry-After, zero tenant-status Repo query) for TEST-DESIGNER to implement, and flags the wording mismatch itself as a candidate for ORCH to route via ISSUE_QUEUE.md if it judges the requirement text should be corrected.
